rationale: Selected scope (joint, 5 groups) is the complete ResNetConvLayer family: 17 module call sites (stem 7x7 layer model.resnet.embedder.embedder plus layer.0/layer.1 of all 8 ResNetBasicLayers), 3645.5us inclusive = 87.4% of the 4168.5us diagnostic CUDA total. Measured facts motivating the rewrite: the invocation is GPU-bound (execution_timeline-1221e205: 88 kernels, kernel_active_union 4097.5us of a 4176.8us kernel span, only 79.2us gaps, host waiting 2.07ms in cudaDeviceSynchronize per python_runtime-aea48e29), so latency must come down by removing/fusing GPU kernel work. Per target-resources.json, every selected site runs conv -> a separate memory-bound eval-BN kernel (cudnn::bn_fw_inf_1C11_kernel_NCHW; stem 227.4us on 32x64x112x112) -> a separate ReLU clamp kernel on 9 of 17 sites (stem 216.7us); aten::batch_norm costs 428.0us and aten::relu 343.9us of the diagnostic CUDA total. Replacement: each ResNetConvLayer forward becomes one cudnn call. Eval-mode BatchNorm is folded exactly into the conv per output channel (s = gamma/sqrt(var+eps), W' = W*s, b' = beta - mu*s, folded once per physical module in float64, stored float32; original parameter tensors stay untouched so the parent fallback stays valid), then conv+bias+ReLU is evaluated by aten.cudnn_convolution_relu (present in the worker's torch 2.13.0+cu129, CUDA dispatch verified) on the 9 ReLU sites, and conv+bias via conv2d on the 8 nn.Identity sites; both preserve the frozen FP32 policy (the fused op runs with TF32 and benchmark disabled, matching torch.backends.cudnn settings). This is a module-boundary replacement only: with the legacy binding backend the direct callable boundaries add no functional-dispatch cost to unrelated operators, and no CUDA graphs are captured. Numerics: BN folding is exact in real arithmetic and only reassociates FP32 rounding; a CPU check of the same formula against conv+BN+ReLU shows max relative error ~2e-7 per layer, orders of magnitude inside the atol=rtol=1e-4 logits tolerance, so exact top-1 and the +1-corruption negative control are expected to hold; observe()'s repeated forward uses the same replacement, keeping its closeness check apples-to-apples. Hypothesis (not a measured clean-timing result): removing the separate BN kernel at all 17 sites and the separate ReLU kernel at 9 sites removes roughly 600us of memory-bound GPU passes (minus any conv-kernel differences from the bias/ReLU epilogue), projecting latency_ms from the clean baseline 4.251697 toward ~3.5-3.7ms; the framework's independent paired measurement decides acceptance. Risks hedged in code: if the fused engine declines or errors for any shape the site latches to conv2d(W',b')+relu (still eliminating the BN kernel), and a per-invocation guard falls back to the parent forward on unexpected signature/dtype/device, training mode or grad-requiring inputs. No inputs/previous-feedback.txt was supplied, so no prior-attempt correction applies; there are no installed bundles to replace or require.

setup_work.where: build() at installation, after adapter.prepare() and before validation; never inside the timed invocation
steps: 1. Per selected ResNetConvLayer module: read conv/normalization/activation, validate layout (Conv2d + eval BatchNorm2d with affine+track_running_stats, ReLU or Identity activation, fp32 CUDA weights) and fold the eval BN into conv weights in float64, casting to contiguous float32 packed tensors (W', b'). Original parameter tensors are left untouched so parent fallback remains the exact original computation.

2. One installation probe of aten.cudnn_convolution_relu on a 1x1x4x4 dummy (under no_grad, followed by torch.cuda.synchronize) to detect setup-level fused-op unavailability; on decline, ReLU sites permanently route to conv2d_folded+relu and report the setup failure category via record_route labels at call time.

retained_setup_memory.note: 10,994,880 folded weight floats + 3,904 folded bias floats retained for the invocation lifetime; counted in framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes (which includes installation), not in the per-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes counter, which is reset for each run.

setup_work.transient_setup_memory: float64 folding intermediates bounded by the largest single conv (64x64x3x3 ~0.3MB), freed during setup; no inference-mode tensors are created (no_grad only), no CUDA graphs or graph pools, no changes to batch/sequence/sampling semantics.
setup_work.expected_run_memory_effect: Per-run peak_allocated should fall versus baseline 281,975,808 bytes because the separate eval-BN output and ReLU output tensors at 17 sites disappear (e.g. two ~102.8MB stem intermediates); this is a PyTorch allocator counter change, not a claim of general physical-memory saving, and the memory metric is non-objective with a 0.95 throughput floor.

quality_risks: FP32 reassociation drift from BN folding (fold computed in float64, cast once): CPU verification of the identical formula shows ~2e-7 max relative error per layer; through 17 layers plus the untouched classifier this is expected to stay orders of magnitude below the atol=rtol=1e-4 logits tolerance, with identical argmax(-1) unless the reference logits contain exact near-ties (not observed; the +1-corruption control is unaffected because it compares our logits to themselves plus one).

cudnn may service the fused conv+bias+ReLU pattern with a different engine than the unfused conv for some shape (notably the 7x7 stride-2 stem), making that site slower than baseline; mitigations: per-site runtime exception fallback to conv2d(W',b')+relu, and the tunable conv_route parameter lets the TaskSearch loop compare the fully-fused and conv2d_folded implementations on paired project measurements before publication.

Route/coverage reporting: replacements self-report via context['record_route'] labels (aten.cudnn_convolution_relu / conv2d_folded(+relu) / setup:fused_unavailable-> / fused_runtime_error-> / parent:*) as diagnostics only; the 17 module replacements are directly invoked each forward, and no CUDA Graph replay is used, so Python replacement invocations remain observable to the framework's coverage accounting.

Eliminated inner calls (162 call IDs listed in eliminated_calls) are the convolution/normalization/activation submodule calls, their aten.functional counterparts (17 conv2d, 17 batch_norm, 9 relu) and the nested opop profiler record-enter/exit instrumentation under the 17 replaced boundaries. Their consumers remain valid because the replacement returns the same NCHW fp32 contiguous tensor the parent produced (torch.equal-verified fallback path; fused path allocates a fresh contiguous output), so the downstream ResNetBasicLayer residual add (hidden_state += residual), MaxPool2d, AdaptiveAvgPool2d and classifier operate unchanged; running-stat buffers of the folded BNs are no longer read, which is exact in eval mode where they are constants, and eval() is re-asserted by adapter.reset().

If any site's layout did not validate at build time, that site is simply omitted from the returned mapping and keeps its parent (reported via replacement_calls differing from the declared 17); on this frozen environment all 17 ResNetConvLayer sites validate by construction.

params.name: conv_route
params.description: Implementation route for the 17 folded conv(+bias) sites: 'cudnn_conv_relu' uses the single fused aten.cudnn_convolution_relu kernel on the 9 ReLU sites (conv2d with folded bias on the 8 Identity sites); 'conv2d_folded' uses conv2d(W', b') plus a separate relu kernel on ReLU sites. Both are quality-equivalent (identical fold, FP32, TF32 off); the choice only selects between two legal implementations and never changes batch, workload, sampling or thresholds. Read from context['parameters']; default 'cudnn_conv_relu'.
